title: Beyond the Visual: The Impacts of Urban Soundscapes on Landscape Design and User Experience

findings.source: Abstract
findings.quote: The purpose of this research is to examine how visual stimuli affect an individual’s perception of the soundscape.

findings.consequent: Aesthetically pleasing spaces that align with urban sounds

minimum_safe_summary: This mixed-methods empirical study investigated how visual stimuli influence the perception of urban soundscapes at Klyde Warren Park in Dallas, Texas. Using on-site user surveys, expert interviews, observational data, and sound-level readings, the research found a positive correlation between auditory and visual stimuli. Key findings indicate that traffic noise, "people" sounds, and water are primary aural elements, while traffic, greenery, and water are leading visual elements impacting soundscape experiences. More visible traffic tends to make the soundscape less pleasant, whereas water and vegetation contribute to a more enjoyable perception, often by psychologically masking unwanted noise. Limitations include the study's cross-sectional nature, specific data collection timeframe, and the challenge of comparing exact sound sources with different visual elements in a real-world setting.
